persons.name: Cakrapāṇi
persons.evidence: likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā cakrapāṇI śarmaṇā

notes: The catalogue field says ŚS 1674, but the colophon reads śāke 1647 (the digits look swapped in the catalogue). ŚS 1647 + 78 = 1725 CE. The month is only given as a number (12), and the pakṣa is not stated. If months are counted from Caitra, month 12 is Phālguna, which would put the date in about Feb–Mar 1726 CE. Weekday 2 is probably Monday. The colophon reads 'likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā(t) cakrapāṇiśarmaṇā sudhiyā': Cakrapāṇi either copied the MS himself or obtained it from someone else. So he is clearly the owner, but he may not be the scribe. 'sudhiyā' (sudhī, 'the wise') is a descriptive word, not a title. The two bhūtasaṃkhyā phrases are verse counts, not dates: vahni(3)-bāṇa(5)-nayana(2) = 253 ślokas in the Sārāvalī, and bāṇa(5)-nanda(9)-nayana(2) = 295 in the anuṣṭubh metre. Both are read correctly.
